ipv4.reference: common line-oriented logging commands (logging host, logging trap, logging facility, logging source-interface); RFC 5424 severities
ipv4.does: Sends the device's log messages, informational and more severe, to Woodshed over TCP.
ipv4.text:
! Enter in global configuration mode, fill in the placeholders, then save the configuration
logging host 10.1.0.50 <TCP-OPTION>
logging trap informational

parts.title: Enter in global configuration mode, fill in the placeholders, then save the configuration
parts.text:
logging host 10.1.0.50 <TCP-OPTION>
logging trap informational

notes: Reference only: not tested on a device; check your device's documentation.

Before you turn on TCP or TLS logging on a firewall: some firewalls block traffic through them when a TCP or TLS syslog server can't be reached, or its certificate fails, unless a "permit traffic when the log host is down" option is set. Check that option first, or use UDP.

<TCP-OPTION> is the device's way of saying TCP to port 514 on the host line. It differs between devices (a transport keyword with a port, a protocol/port pair after the address, or a separate command), so take it from the device's documentation.
`logging trap` sets the lowest severity sent to log hosts on many devices; others set it on the host line, or accept the number (6) instead of the keyword.
Turn on timestamps in the messages if the device offers it (with milliseconds and the time zone, where it can); Woodshed also keeps the time each message arrived.
ipv4.check: The device appears on Woodshed's Dashboard with its first message; if it doesn't, check the device's log host status and Woodshed's Listeners on the Setup page.

ipv4.reference: common set-style syslog statements (set system syslog host …); RFC 5424 severities and facilities
ipv4.does: Sends the device's log messages, informational and more severe, to Woodshed over TCP.
ipv4.text:
! Enter in configuration mode, then commit
set system syslog host 10.1.0.50 any info
set system syslog host 10.1.0.50 port 514
set system syslog host 10.1.0.50 transport tcp
set system syslog host 10.1.0.50 structured-data
commit

parts.title: Enter in configuration mode, then commit
parts.text:
set system syslog host 10.1.0.50 any info
set system syslog host 10.1.0.50 port 514
set system syslog host 10.1.0.50 transport tcp
set system syslog host 10.1.0.50 structured-data
commit

notes: Reference only: not tested on a device; check your device's documentation.

Before you turn on TCP or TLS logging on a firewall: some firewalls block traffic through them when a TCP or TLS syslog server can't be reached, or its certificate fails, unless a "permit traffic when the log host is down" option is set. Check that option first, or use UDP.
`any info` sends every facility at info and above; the facility and level keywords differ slightly between devices.
`structured-data` asks for RFC 5424 messages where the device offers it; leave the line out if it doesn't.
Not every set-style device can send syslog over TCP, and those that can don't all use a `transport` statement: check the documentation before you rely on it.
Set the address the messages come from with `set system syslog source-address <address>` if the device has several; Woodshed shows that address as the device.
ipv4.check: The device appears on Woodshed's Dashboard after the commit, with its first message.
